primary_diagnosis: Uncontrolled resistant hypertension with early target-organ damage
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with severe diastolic hypertension (BP 142/117) despite monotherapy, multiple atherogenic lipid abnormalities, pre‑diabetes, and chronic borderline anemia. These findings, together with rising BUN and missing renal protection, point to resistant hypertension as the dominant problem, with early target‑organ impact. The risk factor profile also supports subclinical coronary disease, occult GI blood loss, OSA, metabolic‑syndrome progression, early CKD, and secondary hypertension. Data gaps (eGFR, urine ACR, iron studies, sleep assessment, thyroid panel) limit certainty for several secondary diagnoses, prompting a broad differential and targeted work‑up.

recommended_workup: 24‑hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) to confirm resistant hypertension
Iron studies (serum ferritin, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation) plus FIT or colonoscopy for occult GI bleed
Serum creatinine with eGFR calculation and urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio
STOP‑Bang questionnaire followed by home sleep apnea test or polysomnography
Plasma renin activity and aldosterone level (aldosterone‑renin ratio) for secondary hypertension
Coronary calcium scoring (CT) to assess subclinical atherosclerosis
Transthoracic echocardiogram with diastolic function parameters and BNP/NT‑proBNP
Ankle‑brachial index (ABI) for peripheral arterial disease
12‑lead ECG and, if negative, 30‑day Holter monitor for atrial fibrillation
PHQ‑9 and GAD‑7 questionnaires for depression/anxiety screening
TSH and free T4 for thyroid function
Serum vitamin B12, methylmalonic acid, and folate levels
Liver panel (ALT, AST, GGT) and abdominal ultrasound or FibroScan for NAFLD
Complete platelet count, MPV, and repeat PDW to evaluate platelet activation
